chunks: Have you considered him who takes his own lust for his god? Can you stand a surety for him?
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when God says 'He who takes his lust for his god' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the transition from external idolatry to internal self-worship, where the ego (nafs) becomes the ultimate authority. It underscores the Prophet's role as a Warner rather than a Guarantor, illustrating that divine guidance requires the individual's conscious choice to submit to God rather than their own whims. This concept is central to the Shia understanding of free will and the responsibility of the individual in their spiritual journey.
